title: Best Invoicing Software in Singapore 2026: HitPay vs Stripe vs Airwallex
summary: Compare the best invoicing software for Singapore SMBs in 2026. HitPay vs Stripe vs Airwallex — payment methods, fees, PayNow support, and payout speed.
body_text: Quick Answer: HitPay is the leading invoicing and payment platform for Singapore SMBs, supporting PayNow, GrabPay, ShopeePay, cards, and BNPL with zero monthly fees and next business day SGD payouts. Stripe and Airwallex also serve Singapore merchants but are better suited to developer-led or globally-focused teams. HitPay is MAS-licensed (PS20200643) and free to sign up, with approval in 1–3 business days. Invoicing is a cash flow problem before it is a software problem. Singapore SMBs — from Tanjong Pagar service firms to Bugis boutique retailers — routinely wait 14–30 days on unpaid invoices. The right invoicing tool closes that gap by embedding a payment link directly into the invoice, so clients pay on the spot rather than by bank transfer later. The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) requires all payment service providers operating in Singapore to hold a valid licence under the Payment Services Act. That regulatory baseline matters when choosing an invoicing platform: unlicensed tools may accept card numbers but cannot settle funds directly into a Singapore bank account without a licensed intermediary. This comparison covers three platforms — HitPay, Stripe, and Airwallex — on the criteria that matter most to Singapore SMBs: invoicing features, local payment method support, fees, and payout speed. What Should a Singapore Invoicing Platform Actually Do? A basic invoicing tool generates a document. A payment-ready invoicing platform does more: Embeds a payment link that accepts PayNow, cards, and wallets Settles funds directly to a Singapore bank account Supports partial payments or deposit collection Sends automated payment reminders Reconciles payments against invoices automatically For B2B invoicing specifically — common among creative agencies, logistics operators, and professional services firms — the ability to collect via PayNow or bank transfer without manual follow-up is the primary time-saver. As covered in the invoice payment guide for Singapore SMEs , embedding a payment link in every invoice reduces average collection time significantly. How Does HitPay Handle Invoicing for Singapore Businesses? HitPay’s invoicing feature is built into its core payment platform. Merchants create and send invoices directly from the HitPay dashboard, and each invoice carries an embedded payment link. Clients can pay via PayNow, GrabPay, ShopeePay, Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Atome, ShopBack PayLater, Apple Pay, or Google Pay — whichever method they prefer. For businesses dealing with international clients, HitPay also accepts cross-border wallet payments including WeChatPay (China), UPI (India), PromptPay (Thailand), DuitNow (Malaysia), and QRIS (Indonesia) — all settled into a Singapore SGD account. Settlement is next business day for domestic SGD transactions. Cross-border payments settle at T+2. There are no monthly fees or setup fees — merchants pay per transaction only. See hitpayapp.com/pricing for current card rates. HitPay also allows merchants to customise payment receipts and invoices with branding, itemised line items, and tax fields — relevant for GST-registered businesses. HitPay is MAS-licensed (PS20200643) and PCI DSS compliant. Approval takes 1–3 business days with no setup fee. How Do Stripe and Airwallex Compare on Invoicing? Does Stripe support invoicing in Singapore? Stripe offers invoicing through Stripe Billing, which supports PayNow, GrabPay, cards, Apple Pay, and Google Pay in Singapore. It is a strong option for developer-led teams that want to customise invoice flows via API. Stripe has no monthly fee and operates on a per-transaction model. The tradeoff: Stripe’s invoicing configuration requires developer time for custom setups. Out-of-the-box invoice customisation for non-technical merchants is more limited than HitPay’s dashboard-native approach. Does Airwallex support invoicing in Singapore? Airwallex offers payment links and bill pay features but its core strength is multi-currency treasury, expense management, and corporate cards. Its Explore plan is free; paid tiers start at SGD 79/month. For Singapore SMBs whose primary need is domestic invoice collection with PayNow, the subscription cost adds friction that per-transaction models avoid. Airwallex is best suited to businesses that also need multi-currency accounts, international transfers, or expense management alongside invoicing — not for merchants primarily collecting SGD invoices locally. Side-by-Side Comparison: Invoicing Platforms for Singapore SMBs Feature HitPay Stripe Airwallex Monthly fee None None From SGD 0 (paid tiers from SGD 79/mo) PayNow support ✅ ✅ Limited GrabPay / ShopeePay ✅ GrabPay only ❌ BNPL (Atome, ShopBack) ✅ ❌ ❌ Cross-border wallets ✅ (WeChatPay, UPI, QRIS, PromptPay, DuitNow) WeChatPay, Alipay Limited Invoice dashboard (no-code) ✅ Requires Stripe Billing setup ✅ Next business day SGD payout ✅ Standard schedule Varies MAS-licensed ✅ (PS20200643) ✅ ✅ Approval time 1–3 business days Varies Varies Best for SMBs needing local e-wallets, PayNow, BNPL, zero monthly fees Developer teams needing API-first invoicing Businesses needing multi-currency treasury + invoicing Which Invoicing Platform Is Right for Singapore SMBs? For most Singapore SMBs — a Tiong Bahru fitness studio collecting class deposits, a Jurong East events firm invoicing corporate clients, or a freelance designer billing via WhatsApp — the decision comes down to three factors: local payment method coverage, fee structure, and how fast funds land in the bank. HitPay covers the full Singapore payment stack with no monthly overhead. For businesses that primarily collect in SGD and want to offer clients PayNow, GrabPay, or BNPL on every invoice, it is the default-fit platform. Stripe is a strong second for technically capable teams that want API control. Airwallex fits businesses that need invoicing as one feature within a broader treasury and spend management stack. For B2B invoicing specifically — where clients may include regional offices paying via DuitNow or PromptPay — HitPay’s cross-border wallet acceptance handles those scenarios without requiring a separate integration. The B2B multi-currency payments guide for Singapore covers this use case in depth. Frequently Asked Questions What is the best invoicing software for small businesses in Singapore? HitPay is the strongest option for most Singapore SMBs because it combines invoice creation, PayNow and GrabPay acceptance, BNPL, and next business day SGD settlement with zero monthly fees. Stripe suits developer-led teams; Airwallex suits businesses needing multi-currency treasury alongside invoicing. Does HitPay support PayNow on invoices in Singapore? HitPay supports PayNow as a payment method on all invoices and payment links in Singapore. Clients receive the invoice with an embedded payment link and can pay via PayNow instantly from any Singapore bank app. Is there a monthly fee for using HitPay's invoicing tool? HitPay charges no monthly fee and no setup fee. Merchants pay per transaction only. Current transaction rates are published at hitpayapp.com/pricing. HitPay vs Stripe for invoicing in Singapore — which is better for a non-technical business owner? HitPay is better for non-technical business owners because invoice creation, payment link embedding, and settlement are all managed through a no-code dashboard. Stripe’s invoicing through Stripe Billing offers more customisation but typically requires developer setup for advanced configurations. How quickly do invoice payments settle with HitPay in Singapore? Domestic SGD invoice payments via HitPay settle next business day into a Singapore bank account. Cross-border payments — such as those made via WeChatPay or PromptPay — settle at T+2. Does Airwallex offer invoicing for Singapore merchants? Airwallex offers payment links and bill pay tools, but its invoicing functionality is secondary to its core treasury and expense management features. Paid plans start at SGD 79 per month, which adds cost for SMBs whose primary need is domestic invoice collection rather than multi-currency operations. Is HitPay licensed to operate as a payment service in Singapore? HitPay is licensed by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) under licence number PS20200643. This licence covers domestic and cross-border payment services in Singapore.

title: Hormone pellets: What to know about HRT pellets for menopause
summary: Learn what hormone pellets are, how they work for menopause therapy, the pros and cons, and what side effects to watch for.
body_text: Hormone pellets are an implanted form of hormone replacement therapy (HRT) that releases estrogen or testosterone gradually over time. It’s one of many hormone therapy options for menopause , and has grown in popularity despite significant debate within the medical community. This guide will help you have a more informed conversation with your care provider about whether or not hormone pellets make sense for you. We'll cover: What hormone pellets are and how they work The types available and their tradeoffs Side effects, safety concerns, and cost How pellets compare to other hormone therapy options Who this approach is and isn't right for Key takeaways Hormone pellets are small implants inserted under the skin that release estrogen or testosterone gradually over three to six months. Most hormone pellets used for menopausal symptoms are compounded, i.e. custom-mixed by a pharmacist, and not FDA-approved for this use. Leading medical organizations, including the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), recommend FDA-approved hormone therapy options over pellet therapy due to limited safety data and the inability to remove a pellet once inserted. Some people find pellets convenient and report symptom relief, but the risks — including hormone overdose and unverifiable potency — are real and worth weighing carefully. A clinician who specializes in hormonal health is your best resource for making an individualized decision. What are hormone pellets? Hormone pellets are a form of hormone replacement therapy (HRT) in which tiny, solid cylinders — slightly larger than a grain of rice — are inserted beneath the skin. Once implanted, they release a steady, low dose of hormones directly into the bloodstream over a period of three to six months. Unlike daily pills or weekly patches, hormone pellets operate on a set-it-and-check-it model: you have the procedure done, and the pellet does its work gradually, without a daily routine to maintain. This convenience factor is a big part of why they've gained traction, particularly among people managing perimenopause symptoms . Hormone pellets are most commonly used to deliver estrogen (in the form of estradiol) or testosterone, and sometimes both. They're used to address symptoms including hot flashes, night sweats, sleep disruption, mood changes, low libido, and vaginal dryness. How hormone pellet therapy works The procedure itself is relatively quick and performed in an outpatient setting. Your care provider numbs a small area — typically on the hip or upper buttock — makes a tiny incision, and inserts the HRT pellet into the subcutaneous tissue (the fat layer just beneath the skin). The incision is then taped closed; no stitches are required. From there, the pellet slowly dissolves and releases hormones into the surrounding tissue and bloodstream. The release rate can vary based on factors like your metabolism, activity level, and overall health, which is part of why absorption is unpredictable from person to person. The pellets themselves don’t need to be removed. They dissolve completely on their own over the course of the treatment period, which typically lasts three to six months. Most formulations available in the U.S. are compounded, i.e. prepared by a licensed compounding pharmacy rather than manufactured by a drug company and reviewed by the FDA. Why choose hormone pellets for menopause treatment Many people exploring menopause treatment options ask whether pellets are more convenient than pills or patches. In some respects, they are. But the presence of reported benefits does not mean pellets are the right or safest choice for everyone. Here's what tends to drive interest: Steady hormone levels. Since pellets release hormones continuously, they don't produce the peaks and troughs associated with daily pills or weekly patches. For some people, this consistency translates to more stable symptom management. Less frequent dosing. A procedure every few months instead of a daily pill or patch you have to remember to change is appealing, especially for people who struggle with routine medication adherence. Interest in "bioidentical" formulations. Compounded hormone pellets are often marketed as bioidentical , meaning their chemical structure is identical to the hormones your body produces naturally. However, "bioidentical" does not mean risk-free. Compounded preparations still carry uncertainty around potency and purity. Symptom relief. Some people report meaningful improvements in hot flashes, sleep, energy, and libido after starting pellet therapy. Types of hormone pellets There are a few different categories of hormone pellets, distinguished by the hormone they contain and how they're formulated. Estrogen and progesterone pellets Estradiol pellets are primarily used to address the classic symptoms of perimenopause and menopause. Estrogen pellets are typically prescribed alongside progesterone for people who still have a uterus. This combination is important because estrogen without progesterone (referred to as "unopposed estrogen") increases the risk of endometrial cancer. Note that there are currently no FDA-approved implantable estradiol pellets available in the U.S. The FDA has found that estradiol pellet formulations can produce unpredictable and fluctuating hormone levels, and has not approved their commercial use for menopausal symptoms. Testosterone pellets Testosterone pellets are used for people experiencing low libido, low energy, and other symptoms associated with declining testosterone levels during midlife. Some providers prescribe them alongside estradiol pellets for a combined approach. There are real usage concerns with testosterone pellets specifically. Because the dose cannot be adjusted once the pellet is inserted, too much testosterone can cause unwanted effects, including acne, oily skin and increased facial hair. Elevated testosterone levels beyond physiological norms after implantation have also been documented as a concern in the medical literature. No FDA-approved testosterone formulation currently exists for managing menopausal symptoms. According to ACOG's guidance , clinicians and patients should use a shared decision-making framework if considering compounded testosterone, and ACOG specifically recommends against pellet delivery due to the lack of safety data and the inability to remove the pellet if problems arise. Custom-compounded pellets Most hormone pellets available in the U.S. are custom-compounded, which means they’re prepared by a licensed compounding pharmacy based on a provider's prescription. Compounding pharmacies play an important role in healthcare by creating formulations for people with specific allergies or needs that standard medications can't meet. However, compounded preparations — including pellets — are not evaluated by the FDA for safety or efficacy in the same way that manufactured drugs are. This means potency, purity, and quality can vary from batch to batch and pharmacy to pharmacy. The National Academy of Sciences has recommended that compounded hormone pellet therapies be considered for restrictions due to concerns about the safety and complexity of the delivery mechanism, and inconsistency in production methods. Pros and cons of hormone pellets It helps to see the tradeoffs clearly before making a decision. Here's an overview of what's known. Potential benefits: Continuous, stable hormone release without daily dosing Convenient since procedure is only required every three to six months Some people report improvements in mood, libido, and energy May provide relief from menopausal symptoms Allows for personalized dosing through compounding Known drawbacks: Most compounded pellets are not FDA-approved Requires a minor surgical procedure with associated recovery Hormone overdose risk, particularly with testosterone, because dosing cannot be adjusted after insertion Side effects including acne, hair growth, mood changes, and breast tenderness Variable absorption and limited long-term safety data Insurance rarely covers the cost Pros Cons Personalized dosing via compounding Not FDA-approved, so not covered by insurance Lasts 3–6 months, no daily routine Minor surgical procedure required May improve mood, libido, and energy Hormone overdose risk, especially with testosterone Can reduce menopausal symptoms Side effects: acne, hair changes, irritability Compounded to individual needs Variable absorption, limited long-term safety data Hormone pellets for women in menopause: What to expect If you and your care provider decide that pellet therapy is appropriate for you, here's a general sense of the timeline. The insertion procedure itself is less than 15 minutes. HRT pellets are placed under the skin through a small incision in the hip or buttock and the site is taped closed. Your care provider will give you specific aftercare instructions, but typically you’ll want to avoid strenuous exercise or submerging the insertion site in water for a few days. Most people notice some initial changes within a few weeks of insertion , though the timeline varies widely. Some feel improved energy and sleep quality relatively quickly, while others experience a more gradual shift over the first month or two. Because everyone's metabolism and starting hormone levels differ, symptom response is highly individual. The effects of hormone pellets for women typically last three to six months , at which point you'd return for another insertion. High levels of stress, vigorous physical activity, and certain medications can increase the absorption rate and may mean you need to return sooner. Side effects and safety concerns What are the side effects of hormone pellets? Common side effects include breast tenderness, acne and oily skin, bloating, mood swings, and — particularly with testosterone — increased hair growth on the face or body. Some people experience temporary discomfort, bruising, or swelling at the insertion site. Less common but more serious risks include infection at the insertion site, pellet extrusion (when the pellet works its way out of the skin), blood clots, and elevated hormone levels beyond what is considered physiologically normal. Estrogen taken without progesterone in someone who still has a uterus carries a risk of endometrial cancer, so progesterone is typically prescribed alongside estradiol-based therapies. The compounding factor adds another layer of uncertainty. Potency and purity can vary because most hormone pellets are not manufactured under FDA oversight. In 2018, the FDA investigated one major hormone pellet manufacturer and identified more than 4,000 adverse events that had not been previously reported to the agency. Among the possible events identified were endometrial cancer, stroke, heart attack, and deep vein thrombosis. How hormone pellets compare to other HRT options Hormone therapy comes in many forms, and pellets are just one of them. Here's how they compare to more commonly used approaches. Pellets Patches Gels/Creams Oral Pills Dosing frequency Every 3–6 months Weekly or twice-weekly Daily Daily FDA approval Not approved (compounded) Approved Approved Approved Dose adjustability Cannot be adjusted after insertion Adjustable Adjustable Adjustable Cost (out-of-pocket) ~$300–$700 per insertion, most insurance won't cover Varies, often partially covered Varies, often partially covered Often lowest cost with insurance Liver impact Bypasses liver Bypasses liver Bypasses liver First-pass liver metabolism Since compounded hormone pellets are not FDA-approved, most insurance plans classify them as elective and will not cover the expense. Annual costs for pellet therapy range from $1,200 to $2,800 for the pellets alone, and that doesn’t include provider visits or lab work. Over time, the total cost is substantially higher than FDA-approved options, which, with insurance, might cost a fraction of that amount annually. FDA-approved options include patches, gels, and oral formulations. These forms of hormone therapy have more established dosing and monitoring guidelines, a longer safety track record, and the flexibility to be modified or discontinued as your needs change. These are meaningful benefits that are worth weighing against the convenience of pellets. Who should (and shouldn't) consider hormone pellet therapy People who may find pellets worth exploring: Those in perimenopause or menopause with persistent, disruptive symptoms that haven't responded well to other hormone therapy delivery methods People who have difficulty maintaining a consistent daily or weekly medication routine Those who have had detailed conversations with a hormone specialist and understand the regulatory and safety context People who should generally avoid hormone pellets: Those with a personal or family history of hormone-sensitive cancers, including breast cancer and certain types of uterine cancer People with a history of blood clots, stroke, or heart attack Those with active liver disease Anyone with unexplained vaginal bleeding (until evaluated by a care provider) People who are pregnant or trying to get pregnant These categories are not intended to be prescriptive. Your individual health history matters more than any general list. The right starting point before making any decision is to seek an evaluation with a care provider who specializes in hormonal health. FAQ What are hormone pellets? Hormone pellets are small, solid implants about the size of a grain of rice that are inserted under the skin and release hormones (typically estradiol, testosterone, or both) steadily into the bloodstream over three to six months. They are a form of hormone replacement therapy used primarily to manage menopausal symptoms and hormone imbalances. Most formulations available in the U.S. are compounded, meaning they are not FDA-approved. Are hormone pellets safe? Some people use hormone pellets without significant problems, and some studies suggest potential symptom relief. However, the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists specifically recommends against pellet therapy because of the lack of safety data and the fact that the pellet cannot be removed if side effects occur or if dosing needs to change. The broader medical consensus from ACOG, the FDA, and the National Academy of Sciences is that FDA-approved hormone therapy options such as pills, patches, or gels/creams have a more established safety profile and should be considered before pursuing compounded pellets. Who is a good candidate for hormone pellets? Hormone pellets may be worth discussing with your care provider if you have persistent menopausal symptoms that haven't responded well to other forms of hormone therapy, and if you have a clear picture of the regulatory and safety landscape. Good candidates are generally those who do not have a history of hormone-sensitive cancers, blood clots, stroke, or liver disease. A thorough evaluation and baseline lab work should always precede this decision. Can hormone pellets help with menopause belly fat? The evidence is limited. Hormonal changes during perimenopause and menopause, particularly declining estrogen, do contribute to shifts in fat distribution such as increased abdominal fat . Hormone therapy in general has been studied in relation to body composition changes during this transition, and some research suggests it may help. However, there is not strong clinical evidence specifically demonstrating that hormone pellets reduce menopause-related abdominal fat. If body composition changes during menopause are a concern for you, a conversation with your care provider about the full range of evidence-based options — including lifestyle factors, diet, and physical activity — is the most useful place to start. How much do hormone pellets cost? Hormone pellet therapy typically costs between $300–$700 per insertion, though prices vary significantly by clinic, geographic location, and the number of pellets needed. Since most people require two to four insertions per year, annual costs for the pellets alone commonly range from $1,200–$2,800. This does not include initial consultation fees, lab work, or follow-up visits, which can add substantially to the total. Since compounded hormone pellets are not FDA-approved, most insurance plans do not cover them. FDA-approved hormone therapy alternatives (patches, gels, and oral medications) are typically far less expensive when covered by insurance.

title: OSS Receives Production Order from Commercial Robotics Customer
summary: ESCONDIDO, Calif. – July 21, 2026 – One Stop Systems, Inc. (OSS or the Company) (Nasdaq: OSS), a leader in rugged Enterprise Class compute for artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML) and sensor processing at the edge, today announced it has received an approximate $2.2 million production order from a manufacturer of autonomous construction and mining equipment. The order follows the successful completion of prototype delivery, testing, and validation, and marks the platform’s transition into production deployment.
body_text: Initial production order valued at approximately $2.2 million Production order follows successful completion of prototype delivery, testing and validation OSS expects cumulative program orders of $10 million to $15 million over the next five years ESCONDIDO, Calif. – July 21, 2026 – One Stop Systems, Inc. (OSS or the Company) (Nasdaq: OSS), a leader in rugged Enterprise Class compute for artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML) and sensor processing at the edge, today announced it has received an approximate $2.2 million production order from a manufacturer of autonomous construction and mining equipment. The order follows the successful completion of prototype delivery, testing, and validation, and marks the platform’s transition into production deployment. Under the order, OSS will deliver its Gen5 ruggedized, 3U, liquid-cooled, short-depth server (SDS), engineered to support commercial autonomous operation of heavy equipment in the construction and mining sectors. Deliveries are expected to begin in the third quarter of 2026 and continue through the third quarter of 2027. OSS continues to anticipate cumulative program orders of $10 million to $15 million over the next five years. “This production order marks an important milestone in our relationship with this autonomous construction and mining equipment manufacturer and reflects the successful transition of this program from prototype development into production deployment,” said Mike Knowles, President and CEO of OSS. “Moving into production reinforces the confidence our customer placed in OSS when they selected us to replace their incumbent compute provider, with our platforms validated through extensive testing in demanding mobile environments. We believe this program demonstrates the growing adoption of our solutions in commercial autonomy platforms and supports our continued growth beyond defense and aerospace markets.” About One Stop Systems One Stop Systems, Inc. (Nasdaq: OSS) is a leader in AI enabled solutions for the demanding 'edge'. OSS designs and manufactures Enterprise Class compute and storage products that enable rugged AI, sensor fusion and autonomous capabilities without compromise. These hardware and software platforms bring the latest data center performance to harsh and challenging applications, whether they are on land, sea or in the air. OSS products include ruggedized servers, compute accelerators, flash storage arrays, and storage acceleration software. These specialized compact products are used across multiple industries and applications, including autonomous trucking and farming, as well as aircraft, drones, ships and vehicles within the defense industry. OSS solutions address the overall AI workflow, from high-speed data acquisition to deep learning, training and large-scale inference, and have delivered many industry firsts for industrial OEM and government customers. As one of the fastest growing segments of the multi-billion-dollar edge computing market, AI enabled solutions require-and OSS delivers-the highest level of performance in the most challenging environments without compromise. OSS products are available directly or through global distributors. For more information, go to www.onestopsystems.com . You can also follow OSS on X , YouTube , and LinkedIn . title: Worthington Enterprises Reports Fourth Quarter and Full-Year Fiscal 2026 Results
summary: Keep current on Worthington Enterprises’ latest developments and find details about our upcoming schedule of events.
body_text: COLUMBUS, Ohio (June 23, 2026) – Worthington Enterprises Inc. (NYSE: WOR), a designer and manufacturer of market-leading building and consumer products that improve everyday life by elevating spaces and experiences, today reported results for its fiscal 2026 fourth quarter and full-year ended May 31, 2026. Recent Developments and Highlights (comparisons to the prior-year period unless otherwise stated) Fourth Quarter fiscal 2026 Net sales were $371.5 million, an increase of 17%, including $44.1 million from recent acquisitions and 3% from organic growth. Net earnings increased to $48.1 million from $3.6 million, while adjusted net earnings were $47.7 million and adjusted EBITDA was $83.5 million. Earnings per share on a fully diluted basis (“EPS – diluted”) improved to $0.97 from $0.08 per share, while adjusted EPS – diluted was $0.97 per share compared to $1.06. Operating cash flow increased $9.2 million to $71.6 million, while free cash flow increased $5.8 million to $55.1 million. Repurchased 350,000 common shares for $18.2 million, leaving 4,565,000 common shares available under the company’s existing repurchase authorization. Declared a quarterly dividend of $0.20 per common share payable on September 29, 2026, to shareholders of record at the close of business on September 15, 2026, representing a 5% increase, or $0.01 per share, compared to the prior quarter. Full-Year fiscal 2026 Net sales were $1.4 billion, an increase of 20%, including $121.7 million from recent acquisitions and 9% from organic growth. Net earnings increased 63% to $155.0 million, while adjusted net earnings increased 8% to $167.6 million and adjusted EBITDA grew 12% to $295.8 million. EPS – diluted improved to $3.14 from $1.92 per share, while adjusted EPS – diluted increased to $3.37 per share from $3.09 per share. Operating cash flow increased 8% to $226.1 million, while free cash flow improved 7% to $170.2 million. Completed the acquisitions of Elgen Manufacturing (“Elgen”) and LSI Group (“LSI”), further expanding the company’s building products portfolio and strengthening its position across the building envelope. “We closed fiscal 2026 with another quarter of solid performance, delivering positive organic growth and strong free cash flow while continuing to execute our strategy,” said Worthington Enterprises President and CEO Joe Hayek. “For the full year, our teams drove double-digit growth in adjusted EBITDA, expanded margins in our wholly owned businesses and maintained a strong balance sheet. I want to thank my colleagues around the world for their continued commitment to serving our customers and delivering value for our shareholders. Their dedication continues to strengthen our business.” View full financial results on our Investor Relations website .

title: Tuya Smart Unveils Upgraded Hey Tuya and Advances Three Core AI Application Ecosystems: AI Home, AI Robot, and AI Energy | news | Tuya Smart
body_text: SHENZHEN, April 23, 2026 — Tuya Smart (NYSE: TUYA, HKEX: 2391), a leading global AI cloud platform service provider, today unveiled its newly upgraded Hey Tuya at the 2026 TUYA Global Developer Summit. Tuya also presented its strategic focus on three core AI application ecosystems: AI Home, AI Robot, and AI Energy. The Summit, which opened today, convened thousands of developers, enterprise representatives, and technology experts from around the world to co-build an AI application ecosystem. Hey Tuya Upgraded: Unlocking New AI Living Experiences The newest version of Hey Tuya represents a comprehensive evolution from foundational AI capabilities to scenario-based intelligent experiences. Third-party services expansion : Hey Tuya now fully integrates with third-party services such as Google Mail, Calendar, and Docs. Users can issue a single voice command to send emails, schedule meetings, or process documents, transforming AI from a conversational tool into an action-oriented assistant. Expanded hardware ecosystem : Hey Tuya has expanded its hardware ecosystem compatibility, with full support for Matter and mainstream open-source platforms such as Home Assistant. Enhanced AI foundation : Hey Tuya’s AI foundation has been comprehensively enhanced to support more natural conversations, deeper reasoning, and complex task planning. Users can speak naturally as they would to a friend, and Hey Tuya interprets intent and completes tasks accordingly, evolving from reactive execution to proactive assistance. Expanded skills : Hey Tuya now includes a rich and continuously expanding skill library, supporting functions such as slide generation, image recognition, image creation, and video generation, better meeting users’ scenario-based needs. Conversational app creation : With Vibe Coding, developers can rapidly build integrated AI+IoT+Web/mobile solutions. Through natural language interaction exclusively, they can create complex scenarios, personalized device control dashboards, lightweight lifestyle applications, and AI-driven automation workflows. This significantly lowers the barrier to AI application development and empowers a broader range of users to realize their creative visions. Scenario-Based Intelligence : The upgraded Hey Tuya supports scenario-based intelligence across use cases including “Morning Wake-up,” “Health Management,” and “Away from Home Protection.” Each scenario is dynamically generated based on user habits, preferences, and real-time conditions. Tuya Expands Full-Stack AI Capabilities for Hardware Innovation In addition to debuting the new version of Hey Tuya, Tuya Smart introduced a suite of self-developed, AI-native technologies purpose-built for real-world hardware deployment. At the Summit, Tuya unveiled its self-trained Personal Voice Activity Detection (PVAD) model, designed specifically for AI hardware scenarios. PVAD enables devices to automatically identify and focus on the intended speaker without prior enrollment, significantly reducing false activations in complex acoustic environments. This allows AI-powered hardware to more accurately determine who is speaking before executing commands, thereby enhancing both reliability and user experience. The company also announced major upgrades and new releases across its AI infrastructure, including Physical AI Foundation V2.8, Wukong AI 3.0, Tuya Real-Time Communication (T-RTC) network, Physical Action Model (PAM), and OmniMem V2.0, a long-term memory system. Together, these technologies form a comprehensive “toolkit” for developers building next-generation AI applications. Attendees also experienced Tuya’s expanding developer ecosystem firsthand. Highlights included TuyaClaw and DuckyClaw, as well as Vibe Coding, which enables developers to build production-grade applications using natural language, and the enhanced Tuya AI development platform. Through this integrated suite of technologies and tools, Tuya is significantly lowering the barrier to AI development, accelerating innovation, and enabling developers worldwide to bring AI-powered applications to market. Tuya Focuses on Three Core AI Application Ecosystems, Co-Creating AI Living with Global Developers At the Summit, Leo Chen, co-chairman and president of Tuya Smart, stated that definitive AI-driven growth has arrived, and almost all hardware is worth rebuilding with AI. Tuya will fully focus on three frontier application domains—AI Home, AI Robot, and AI Energy—empowering developers to unlock AI value and embrace the next decade-defining opportunity with a “Day One” mindset. AI Home : Enable whole-home intelligent coordination and proactive services across devices through AI. AI Robot : Enhance and expand experiences and application scenarios across five categories—companionship, cleaning, wellness, protection, and embodied robotics. AI Energy : Build an AI-driven energy management system for precise energy monitoring, efficient utilization, and intelligent optimization. From a business-to-business AI developer platform to consumer-facing AI applications, the 2026 TUYA Global Developer Summit outlines a clear path for AI to move from technology to real-world application. Looking ahead, Tuya Smart will continue to work with global developers and ecosystem partners to push the boundaries of innovation, accelerate AI adoption, and bring AI into every corner of the physical world.
